{
  "albumInformation": "<p><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Home Recordings. Children singing, screaming and storytelling.</span></p>\n<p><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">All recordings are sourced from cassette tapes found in thrift stores and junk shops, tapes dubbed for us (from two of the kids featured here) and one tape was even found in a gutter! The only exception being the last track on this recording, by Grandpa Norm, singing to his grandson and we thought it fit quite nice on this compilation of home cassette recordings.</span><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Remember when you were a kid? Did you have a recorder? Even if you never held a microphone to your mouth and screamed making funny faces, I'm sure you can recall a time when you jumped around like a silly little monkey hooting and hollering. Maybe you still do! We hope so.</span><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Little is known on the background of these recordings. Estimated recording dates are from the early 1970's to the mid 1990's.</span></p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>Traditional and ecstatic improvisations by L. Gonze</p>\n<p>A work in progress, permently. Songs being added as I make them, removed as my feelings change, or upgraded to better versions when I get an idea. This album will be finished when I stop making changes. But there is no definition of what it means to stop making changes.</p>\n<p>The idea for this series of recordings is:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Start with traditional acoustic americana. Take it out.</li>\n<li>Solo. Just one musician.</li>\n<li>When multitracking only one track has music. Others are found sounds.</li>\n<li>The music track is an improvisation. It's a single take from start to finish - no edits. For example, no comping parts from different takes.</li>\n<li>Introverted.</li>\n</ul>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>\"Halloween is meant to be scary, right? Year after year we dust off the old novelty records. While those oldies are fun, they not at all frightening. Oddio Overplay put the challenge to musical artists the world over to create Halloween music that is 'frightening, damaging and disturbing.' No 'Monster Mash,' instead creepy soundtracks to a fiendish Halloween. They succeeded with CALLING ALL FIENDS! Some of these pieces will creep you right out of your skin.<br /><br />\"Everyone involved in this project hopes you have a thrill ride with this music and <strong>A Scary and Very Happy Halloween!</strong>\"<br /></p><p><span class=\"heado\"><em>source: original release notes on <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.oddiooverplay.com/ears/fiends/\">Oddio Overplay</a></em><br /></span><span class=\"heado\"></span></p><p>[Tracks 5, 19, and 23 are copyright protected and only available on the original website.]</p>",

{
  "albumInformation": "<p><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Home Recordings. Children singing, screaming and storytelling.</span></p>\n<p><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">All recordings are sourced from cassette tapes found in thrift stores and junk shops, tapes dubbed for us (from two of the kids featured here) and one tape was even found in a gutter! The only exception being the last track on this recording, by Grandpa Norm, singing to his grandson and we thought it fit quite nice on this compilation of home cassette recordings.</span><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Remember when you were a kid? Did you have a recorder? Even if you never held a microphone to your mouth and screamed making funny faces, I'm sure you can recall a time when you jumped around like a silly little monkey hooting and hollering. Maybe you still do! We hope so.</span><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Little is known on the background of these recordings. Estimated recording dates are from the early 1970's to the mid 1990's.</span></p>"
}

{

Children singing, screaming and storytelling.</span></p>\n<p><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">All recordings are sourced from cassette tapes found in thrift stores and junk shops, tapes dubbed for us (from two of the kids featured here) and one tape was even found in a gutter! The only exception being the last track on this recording, by Grandpa Norm, singing to his grandson and we thought it fit quite nice on this compilation of home cassette recordings.</span><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Remember when you were a kid? Did you have a recorder? Even if you never held a microphone to your mouth and screamed making funny faces, I'm sure you can recall a time when you jumped around like a silly little monkey hooting and hollering. Maybe you still do! We hope so.</span><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Little is known on the background of these recordings. Estimated recording dates are from the early 1970's to the mid 1990's.</span></p>"
}

  "albumInformation": "<p>\"Halloween is meant to be scary, right? Year after year we dust off the old novelty records. While those oldies are fun, they not at all frightening. {
  "albumInformation": "<p>To hear about future releases, you can join my mailing list, facebook or twitter from my website Axletreewood.com or the links on the artist page here, Thanks for listening :)</p>\n<p> </p>\n<p>Following the kind feedback from the first little EP, here is a second, recorded in the studio this time on a set of rare vintage microphones.</p>\n<p>These songs have emerged out of the spectacular autumn we've had in the UK, growing some vegetables and taking journeys through the countryside, past hamlets and streams, alive with the yellows and reds of the season.</p>\n<p>The artwork features a photo by Ailsa Naumann, (called 'witening wall'), who is also the inspiration for the second piece.</p>\n<p>Instagram: ailsa_naumann</p>\n<p>Enjoy, and feel free to let me know what you've used the pieces for :)</p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>The album \"elevenandtwelve\" was born as a MIDI experiment in 2010. It’s nisei23's second full length release on rec72 and it’s worth that while! Because you’ll see drones and gravity’s rainbow after listening elevenandtwelve, that wild electronic shoe-gazer star. Most of the playing –  synths, pianos, guitars – has been improvised on an iPhone, recorded simultaneously on a computer and edited afterwards. nisei23′s album contains thirteen titles (+5o minutes).</p>"
}

Supplied notices

{
  "albumInformation": "<p><em>Walla walla</em> is the American term for atmospheric crowd background sounds in film and radio. In Japan, it is known as <em>gaya</em>, <em>rhubarb</em> the UK, <em>rhabarber</em> in Germany, and <em>rabarbar</em> in the Belguim, Netherlands, and Scandinavia.</p>\n<p><a href=\"http://www.filmsound.org/terminology/walla.htm\" target=\"_blank\">Film Sound</a> describes it in this way:</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">A sound effect for the murmur of a crowd in the background. </span><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">Walla is often use as subliminal aural communication and  sets a mood or a tone.</span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">The word <em>walla</em> was created in the old radio days when they needed the sound of a crowd in the background. They found if several people simply repeated \"walla, walla, walla, walla\"  it sounded like people talking. The audience did not really hear the words, just the buzz of voices.</span></p>\n</blockquote>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">Walla may be field recordings of crowds or staged by actors. This collection features actual groups and crowds recorded all over the world and generously donated for reuse at <a href=\"http://www.freesound.org\" target=\"_blank\">Freesound.org</a>. </span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">Such recordings may be helpful to and appreciated by FMA visitors creating audio and video productions. The recordings have been normalized, standardized for bitrates, tagged, and converted to mp3s from various other formats for this Free Music Archive collection. Please see individual tracks for licensing.<br /></span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\"> </span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\"><em>total time: 1:24:06</em><br /></span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">cover painting </span><span class=\"fn\"><em>Манифестация 17 октября 1905 года<strong> (</strong></em></span><em>Demonstration on October 17, 1905) by Ilya Repin (1844-1930)</em><span class=\"fn\"><em><strong><br /></strong></em></span></p>"
}

In Japan, it is known as <em>gaya</em>, <em>rhubarb</em> the UK, <em>rhabarber</em> in Germany, and <em>rabarbar</em> in the Belguim, Netherlands, and Scandinavia.</p>\n<p><a href=\"http://www.filmsound.org/terminology/walla.htm\" target=\"_blank\">Film Sound</a> describes it in this way:</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">A sound effect for the murmur of a crowd in the background. </span><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">Walla is often use as subliminal aural communication and  sets a mood or a tone.</span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">The word <em>walla</em> was created in the old radio days when they needed the sound of a crowd in the background. They found if several people simply repeated \"walla, walla, walla, walla\"  it sounded like people talking. The audience did not really hear the words, just the buzz of voices.</span></p>\n</blockquote>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">Walla may be field recordings of crowds or staged by actors. This collection features actual groups and crowds recorded all over the world and generously donated for reuse at <a href=\"http://www.freesound.org\" target=\"_blank\">Freesound.org</a>. </span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">Such recordings may be helpful to and appreciated by FMA visitors creating audio and video productions. The recordings have been normalized, standardized for bitrates, tagged, and converted to mp3s from various other formats for this Free Music Archive collection. Please see individual tracks for licensing.<br /></span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\"> </span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\"><em>total time: 1:24:06</em><br /></span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">cover painting </span><span class=\"fn\"><em>Манифестация 17 октября 1905 года<strong> (</strong></em></span><em>Demonstration on October 17, 1905) by Ilya Repin (1844-1930)</em><span class=\"fn\"><em><strong><br /></strong></em></span></p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p><strong>[fm.m02] </strong>field muzick mini cdr serie<br /></p><p>This psychoactive acoustical survey sets out to explore, under which  circumstances sounds and noises from the street cease to annoy.                               <br /><br /><em>»Like a sky-coloured Sunday-morning version of Kraftwerk’s \"Autobahn\".« Tocafi </em></p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>...These recordings took place at the IRCAM Paris in October of 2005. I  drove there in a Citroen CX. For whatever reason, the Plugins of my  Sequencer Software started to melt. This slowed down the recording  process in such a way, that I embarked on my journey home empty-handed.  Just like in a dream.</p>\n</blockquote>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>A neo-funk rock band De ImperfAction brought together a group of talented aspiring musicians from four continents. Their compositions reflect a wide range of social injustice: they speak up about growing lack of privacy on a planet; about the enormous amount of rape and murder in the world; about our hardened unholy generation; about people becoming social toys, about the losers and wanna-be ones; about disconnection and desolation of a modern man, lost and outcast.  <br /><br />Their style is a quirky mix of a heavy funk with the bits of rapping set on the Baroque period influenced harmonies.</p>"
}

  "albumInformation": "<p>This is an ambient electronic noise album that looks at our connection to technology and issues of our personal privacy or lack thereof.  </p>\n<p>Dedicated to those defending our rights to privacy and freedom. </p>\n<p>Visit, Learn, Donate @ <a href=\"http://www.freeross.org\" target=\"_blank\">www.freeross.org</a> - <a href=\"http://www.eff.org\" target=\"_blank\">www.eff.org</a></p>\n<p> </p>\n<p><span style=\"text-decoration: underline;\">Credits</span> </p>\n<p><strong>eric “eroctech” toledo</strong> - guitars, keys, programing, recording, and mixing using ableton live </p>\n<p><strong>canelo “the pug”</strong> – paws on wood floor, barking, final mix approval </p>\n<p> </p>\n<p>“Miles Copeland (The Program)”</p>\n<p>remix from “Mixtape 02”</p>\n<p>called “Miles Copeland (Red Dawn)” </p>\n<p> </p>\n<p>\"Radio Transmissions\" </p>\n<p><strong>eric \"eroctech\" toledo</strong> - guitars, drum programing, recording & mixing </p>\n<p><strong><a href=\"http://bionix.bandcamp.com\" target=\"_blank\">bIONIX</a></strong> - ni maschine played live </p>\n<p> </p>\n<p>[<a href=\"http://music.theblackpenguins.com/album/everything-in-ones-and-zeros\" target=\"_blank\">Source</a>. <a href=\"http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/\" target=\"_blank\">CC BY</a>]</p>"

{
  "albumInformation": "<p style=\"margin-bottom:0in;line-height:100%;\"> To those who examine the themes in my work it is likely no surprise to hear that a lot of my motivation comes from philosophical and political beliefs – though to this point, I believe a lot has been left ambiguous or softened such that it might be enjoyed regardless of your personal convictions.</p>\n<p>It's without regret or reservation that I present this new collection – the creation of which has been a necessary respite from the realities of the world as it is today. These are loud, angry songs that come from louder, angrier thoughts – and it is my hope that by making these songs I have drawn out some of the venom that brought them about.</p>\n<p style=\"margin-bottom:0in;line-height:100%;\">I hope folks can find some comfort in these songs, and that the creators among you might put them to good use.</p>\n<p> </p>\n<p style=\"margin-bottom:0in;line-height:100%;\"> </p>\n<p> </p>\n<p> </p>\n<p style=\"margin-bottom:0in;line-height:100%;\"> </p>\n<p> </p>"

  "albumInformation": "<p>We made our music available under the Creative Common license BY, but would like to add the non existing code ‘NAD'NAD stands for \"No Audio Derivates’In other words you can freely use (part of) our tracks in a film or video, but cannot remix or re-use part of our tracks in other musical work without our permission. We’d appreciate it if you could let us know where/when you used our music.As an extra service we can make custom edits or mixes for you. You can choose fragments, loops, solo-ed instruments, remixes, etc.Please feel free to contact us if you want to know more about using and/or customising our music  in your project.</p>\n<p>Unheard Music Concepts: purely improvised instrumental music. A mixture of jazz, classical and minimal music with a touch of electronics.Unheard Music Concepts is a trio from the Netherlands consisting of Han Post (sax, clarinet), Marc Verhoeven (keys) and Daniel Talma (upright bass).They played together for many years in several groups (the Urge, Two Gentlemen, Masters & Johnson, Dutch Distress) and decided to go back to what they think is the core of all music: communication.They meet and play. They don't agree on chords, tempo or anything else. It is all about listening to and interacting with each other.Everything is recorded on a simple multitrack recorder, afterwards the best pieces are selected and mixed.Two albums have been released; Harbour (2015) and Industry (2016)</p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>This is a dark ambient requiem for a soul in the process of shattering. It draws thematically from Ingmar Bergman's similarly titled  movie whose female protagonist suffers from schizophrenia. Sampled  lines from the main character's monologues/dialogues with God are used  as material in the track. There is similar choral material here that can  be found in Doc &amp; Lena's Cosmic Lullabies  album but instead of serving as spacious meditative background it  serves here a more intense and darker role together with processed  saxophone sounds and a church organ.</p>\n<p>- <a href=\"http://www.jamendo.com/en/album/21707\" target=\"_blank\">Jamendo</a></p>"

  "albumInformation": "<p>Started in March of 2009 by Jerry Cooper, an avid guitar player with 40+ years of experience. While blues is his main drive, any genre that uses a guitar can benefit from his creativity.Greg Pappas (originally born in Cancun, Mexico and now living in Zaragoza, Spain) was at this time the vocalist for this group. Known as the \"Chairman of the Board\" in Spain, he is known worldwide for his powerful vocals, inspiring lyrics, and speed painting. Please reference his videos on YouTube.Frank Nelson joined our group in August of 2009 with the intent of completing some projects which had become stalled. He helped put the projects together, reconstructing the drum tracks & adding keyboard tracks as necessary. Mixdown & mastering of the project was also handled by him.Greg left us a couple of months later. He stays pretty busy. But we managed to get noticed by another vocalist.Brad Wilson joined our group & did most of the vocals for the rest of this ongoing project. Ha also added some amazing harmonica tracks to a lot of our songs. He is currently a member of our band and we hope he stays with us for a long time to help us with our ongoing project.</p>"

  "albumInformation": "<div class=\"tralbumData tralbum-about\">.zigo is a sound artist from Argentina and he has been recording, playing, improvising, taking photographs and filming his own travels around the world since the mid 80s, when he was immersed in the world of cassette culture. <br /><br /> 'Acrolitos' is the fifth of the Industria Tropical series of EPs by artists who published on the <a href=\"https://pakapirecords.bandcamp.com/album/va-industria-tropical\" target=\"_blank\">Industria Tropical compilation</a>. <br /> <br /> Here he creates an earthly soundscape where tropical beats gets cold and suspended in echoed dreams filled with insects and electronic waves brings a nocturnal, haloed warmth.</div>"
}

{
  "track_information": "For this week's Junto, the goal was to take pre-existing field recordings and to turn them into something else. The pre-existing field recordings are the audio produced by Disquiet Junto members for projects 0037 and 0038. Here are the two I used:\n\nAscension: Macy's Escalator [disquiet0037-asrealasitgets1] by Super Miracle Dream Team\n\nPost [disquiet0037-asrealasitgets1] by Lem Herlihy\n\nThe field recordings in question are documents of retail spaces, such department stores. We were told to rework the audio from one or more of the field recordings to achieve something inspired by the following description: \"There was the continuous roar of the machine at work, of customers crowding into the departments, dazzled by the merchandise, then propelled towards the cash-desk. And it was all regulated and organized with the remorselessness of a machine: the vast horde of women were as if caught in the wheels of an inevitable force.\" The quote comes from the novel Au Bonheur des Dames, or The Ladies' Paradise, by Émile Zola, originally published in 1883.\n\nI found the more rhythmically and texturally interesting elements in the two recordings, mostly sounds of escalators and a forklift backing up. Some muzak also found its way in. I used my entire bag of Ableton tricks to impose beats and tonality.\n\nThis Disquiet Junto project was done in association with the exhibit As Real as It Gets, organized by Rob Walker at the gallery Apex Art in Manhattan (November 15 - December 22, 2012):\n\nhttp://apexart.org/exhibitions/walker.php/\n\nMore on this 43rd Disquiet Junto project at:\n\nhttp://disquiet.com/2012/10/25/disquiet0043-dazzledmachine/\n\nMore details on the Disquiet Junto at:\nhttp://soundcloud.com/groups/disquiet-junto/info",
  "albumInformation": "<p>Two remixes with mechanical intent made from soundscapes from retail spaces<br /><br />Two soundscapes from a retail space.<br /><br />Two artificially created soundscapes of imaginary retails spaces.<br /><br />This is a sampler of the 1500+ tracks submitted to the Disquiet Junto thus far, curated by Marc Weidenbaum of Disquiet.com. <a title=\"http://freemusicarchive.org/member/jason/blog/Disquiet_Junto_ApexArt_Interview_Marc_Weidenbaum\" href=\"/member/jason/blog/Disquiet_Junto_ApexArt_Interview_Marc_Weidenbaum\" target=\"_blank\">FMA Interview 11/24/2012</a>.</p>\n<p><strong><em>From <a href=\"http://disquiet.com\" target=\"_blank\">Disquiet.com</a></em></strong>: The Disquiet Junto is an ongoing weekly collaborative music-making space from Disquiet.com in which restraints are used as a springboard for creativity. It's housed at <a href=\"http://soundcloud.com/groups/disquiet-junto/discussion\">soundcloud.com</a>. Subscribe to the announcement list at <a href=\"http://tinyletter.com/disquiet-junto\">tinyletter.com/disquiet-junto</a>.</p>\n<p>These are the weekly projects to date: <a {
  "albumInformation": "<p>Mudboy (aka Raphael Lyon) hails from Providence, RI. He plays the Mudboy Mini, a custom-built air organ/Yamaha FM mod synth hybrid. Details are <a href=\"http://www.mudboymusic.com/secrets.html\">here</a>, and he'll make one for you if you like. He also runs the <a href=\"http://freematterfortheblind.com/\">Free Matter for the Blind</a> record label, dealing in \"Strange Sounds for Strange People\". The label does limited releases with hand-made artwork, and once they're gone, many of them will be available for download from the <a href=\"http://freemusicarchive.org/\">Free Music Archive</a>. I posted a sampling of Mudboy's music in last week's <a href=\"http://blog.wfmu.org/freeform/2008/06/pissin-in-the-p.html\">Providence FMA preview</a>, and some more Free Matter for the Blind audio is available for download after the jump in this here post. (-by Jason Sigal)</p>\n<p><a href=\"http://www.wfmu.org/playlists/shows/27538\">http://www.wfmu.org/playlists/shows/27538</a></p>"

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>Steve Combs and Simon Mathewson have expanded on the partnership resulting in their <a href=\"http://freemusicarchive.org/music/Steve_Combs/Notes/\"> Notes album</a>, yielding what we believe is the largest musical collaboration among Free Music Archive artists. Enlisting a dozen musicians with diverse backgrounds from the FMA, Steve set up a framework for random collaboration on the dozen tracks comprising the album. With three musicians per track, assigned to either start, continue or finish their piece, we present a set of audio <a href=\"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exquisite_corpse\">exquisite corpses</a>.</p>\n<p>To represent the random assemblage comprising the music, the album art is constructed with tiles provided by each participant.</p>\n<p>Produced, mixed and mastered by <a href=\"http://freemusicarchive.org/music/Lee_Rosevere/\" target=\"_self\">Lee Rosevere</a></p>\n<p><strong>I Know It’s Raining, Let’s Hug Anyway </strong>by Candlegravity, Unthunk, and simon_mathewson</p>\n<p><strong>If That’s What You Want</strong> by Steve Combs, half cocked, and Unthunk</p>\n<p><strong>Tessera</strong> by Blue Dot Sessions, Scott Holmes, and half cocked</p>\n<p><strong>Turkish Delight</strong> by half cocked, Blue Dot Sessions, and Small Colin (Ft. Lee Rosevere on drums)</p>\n<p><strong>Eat My Shorts</strong> by Scott Holmes, Small Colin, and Matt Oakley</p>\n<p><strong>Sleepless</strong> by Jahzzar, Candlegravity, and Blue Dot Sessions</p>\n<p><strong>Trident</strong> by simon_mathewson, Steve Combs, and Jahzzar</p>\n<p><strong>Unconquered Sun</strong> by Matt Oakley, simon_mathewson, and Scott Holmes</p>\n<p><strong>Loops To Aviemore</strong> by Small Colin, Matt Oakley, and Aglow Hollow</p>\n<p><strong>Mach Precedent</strong> by Aglow Hollow, Monk Turner, and Candlegravity</p>\n<p><strong>Baby Babble</strong> by Monk Turner, Aglow Hollow, and Steve Combs</p>\n<p><strong>Veronica’s Lament</strong> by Unthunk, Jahzzar, and Monk Turner</p>\n<p>The cover art was authored by the group as a collective, and is in the public domain under a CC0 license.</p>\n<p>For high-quality formats, download this album from the Bandcamp link.</p>"

{
  "albumInformation": "<div><span style=\"color: #666666; font-family: Helvetica,sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 14px;\">“My mind in space communicating with satellites station,” well something like that. That was one of the first bars from CuzOH’s new EP entitled, “Cuz I Can.” After hearing those lyrics I knew I was in for something different. Different in the way it will be something that I have to listen more than once not because of beats but because of actual lyrics. CuzOH’s lyrics show an ambition to be something better in hip-hop and bring forward a sound we have been missing for a little while now. On my favorite track on the album, Cuz raps about the regular rap subject matter; weed. But even though it’s another weed song it is well down and he uses the new pull of weed to consumers to the way his music will pull people into him and never let go. He says an overdose is good for your soul and he may be right, well of his music.</span></div>\n<p>- ImoveIlive.com</p>"
}

  "albumInformation": "<p><span><span>\"The Mugris es el alter ego de Mauricio Romero, músico residente en Talcahuano y ya cuenta con varias ediciones en cassette y 7”, a traves de sellos independientes como ETCS, BYM, La Resístanse, Discos Cetaceos y No Problema Tapes. Su prontuario incluye presentaciones junto a bandas y músicos como Moon Duo, Bob Bellerue y Luciérnaga (Estados Unidos), Ngly (Alemania), White Sample, Föllakzoid, A Full Cosmic Sound, The Ganjas, Un Festín Sagital, Alejandro Paz, Diegors, entre una larga lista. </span></span><br /><br />La electrónica de The Mugris siempre ha recibido el influjo de la psicodélia y el Krautrock, lo que queda bien manifiesto en pasajes de este nuevo álbum. El vehículo creativo de Mauricio Chispa acaba de completar un Tour por Brasil junto a las bandas A Full Cosmic Sound y Travelling Wave. Esta experiencia sirvió de inspiración para completar \"Super Dog\", trabajo publicado el 11 de septiembre por los sellos Discos Cetáceos y Traición'73.\"</p>"

{
  "albumInformation": "<p style=\"margin: 0px; text-indent: 36.1px; font-size: 12px; font-family: Georgia;\">I traveled from the south of India to Nepal and back again in the winter and spring of 2015.  The experience changed my life.  As much of these recordings are an expression of the place and temperament that is India and Nepal, I believe in a way they tell somewhat of my story, too (though in a different language).  All recordings are raw; only the length of time was edited in any way.  </p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; text-indent: 36.1px; font-size: 12px; font-family: Georgia;\"><em>Volume III </em>is natural.  Soundscapes meant to create a three dimensional space.  Field recordings in the purist sense. </p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>After five years and 37 volumes of the <strong>netBloc</strong> series, I think it’s fair to say that blocSonic has turned on more than a few people to the netaudio culture. From the beginning, that was precisely why I began the series. I strive to make each volume eclectic and packed with information about each track. Combine that with the professionally designed art &amp; PDF and what you’re left with is a compilation that serves as a great way to catch up on what’s been happening in netaudio culture.</p>\n<p>Of course, if you’re new to netaudio, it’s also a great way to introduce you to that very culture. Is this the first netBloc release you’ve come to check out? If so, I welcome you. When you’re done enjoying “netBloc Vol. 37: FIVE”, please check out <a href=\"http://blocsonic.com/releases/type/netblocs\">the other 36 volumes</a>!</p>\n<p>Thanks, also, to all of you who continue to return to blocSonic to enjoy this series! It’s certainly a pleasure to be able to turn you on to incredible, INDEPENDENT music.</p>\n<p>Remember… everything we release is cool to share! Always keep the music moving… share it… blog it… podcast it! If you’re in radio… support independent music and broadcast it!</p>\n<p>Cheers to the next five years!</p>\n<p><strong>Want high-resolution album art, liner-notes or lossless FLAC audio? <a href=\"http://blocsonic.com/releases/show/netbloc-vol-37-five\">Check out the blocSonic release page</a>!</strong></p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>Return to Normal is Corinne and Marty Lucas — we hope you’ll enjoy the Briars and Brome, our third LP. For this collection, we looked back to the traditions of American folk music, and tried to re-imagine the themes and forms we found there in a way that felt both fresh and listenable. <br /><br />On “Old Uncle Cletus” Bryan Ciliberto (Knoxville, Tennessee, USA) plays lead guitar, and Jonas Qvarsebo (Malmö, Sweden) plays drums. Joseph Houck (Boone, North Carolina, USA) plays mandolin on A 21st Century Levee Moan and Wayfaring Stranger. Mark Biegel (Schererville, Indiana, USA) plays trumpet and cornet on The Observer and Coffee with Borges, and Pichy Sotomayor (Buenos Aires, Argentina) co-wrote, and plays lead guitar, bass and programmed the drums for Coffee with Borges. <br /><br />Lyrics by Marty Lucas, except portions traditional. Otherwise, performed, arranged, recorded and mixed by Return to Normal in North Judson, Indiana USA during 2014 and 2015. Additional mixing and mastering by Jon Huxtable at smallfishrecordings in Edinburgh Scotland, UK.</p>\n<p>All three Return to Normal LPs are available as downloads or physical CDs through iTunes, BandCamp, and Amazon. For lots more music and a bit of idle chit-chat visit: https://soundcloud.com/mlucas.</p>"
}

  "albumInformation": "<p><span style=\"color:#212121;\">Modern alienation, yes but lets go further; confusion be our guide again. Once cast on cavestone in the form of wolves and aurochs, we now throw you at garage walls in the shape of animals we know. {
  "albumInformation": "<p><span class=\"article_title_list\"><span class=\"article_title_list\"><b>File under:</b> Electronic Breakbeat Jazz</span></span></p><p><em>From the <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.allaboutjazz.com\">All About Jazz</a> review:</em><br /></p><p><span class=\"article_title_list\"><span class=\"article_title_list\">Combining \nelectronic breaks with jazz improvisation, <span style=\"text-decoration:underline;\">Effects of Elevation</span> is a \nunique example of the interesection where modern jazz and modern \nelectronic music meet.<br /><br />The release features guest musician \nMatthew Garrison on bass. Matt is known for his work with Herbie \nHancock, Joe Zawinul and others. Additionally, track 3 features vocal \nsamples by Ill-esha, known for her work as both a DJ and vocalist.</span></span></p><p> <em><a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.allaboutjazz.com/\">All About Jazz</a> writeup describes the remix, as well.</em><br /><span class=\"article_title_list\"><span class=\"article_title_list\"><br />Citizen\n Prime's remix combines a house groove with piano and bass solos on top.\n The airtight 4-to-the-floor rhythm propels the song as it progresses \nthrough solos, breakdowns and builds.<br /><br />The Sevenless remix \nincorporates IDM, glitch and industrial genres, while retaining a \ndistinctive sound. The remix begins slowly, eventually building into \nepic proportions with a guitar-laden breakbeat chorus.<br /><br /><em>EP info:</em><br /></span></span></p><p>Track 1 written and produced by Jonah Dempcy.\n  </p><p>Track 2 written and produced by <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.corkedfork.com\">Scott Baggett</a>.</p>\n  <p>Track 3 written and produced by <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://nicolas.manel.free.fr\">Nicolas Manel</a>.</p>\n  <p>Vocal sample on track 3 by <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.ill-esha.com\">Ill-esha</a>.</p>\n    <p>Cover art and design by <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.yurikomiyamoto.com\">Yuriko Miyamoto</a>.</p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\">All of the tracks on this adventurous chip music compilation began with <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"monorave.wav\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/monowave.wav\" target=\"_blank\">a single sample</a>.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\">That's the sound of the <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"http://www.vacoloco.net/synths/monowave/\" href=\"http://www.vacoloco.net/synths/monowave/\" target=\"_blank\">Monowave</a>, a Moog clone originally envisioned as a bass synth.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\"><strong>Hexawe</strong>, a <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"Creative Commons - Attribution\" href=\"http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0\" target=\"_blank\">CC-BY</a> label for <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"http://littlegptracker.com/\" href=\"http://littlegptracker.com/\" target=\"_blank\">Piggy Tracker</a> releases, put out an open call for remixes. This group of talented musicians heeded the call, looping tiny sections of the monowave sample and sequencing these instruments using their portable game console of choice. The result is <strong>Monorave</strong>, an inspiring showcase of what's possible with remixed digital soundwaves.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\">This compilation is truly open source in that you can <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\" target=\"_blank\">download the tracker DAT files</a> yourself and tweak them. When you do, you'll find that each song has a folder containing all the samples used in the sequence, and many of the tracks draw all of their source material from that single monowave sample. -<a title=\"http://freemusicarchive.org/member/jason/blog/Monorave_Compilation\" href=\"/member/jason/blog/Monorave_Compilation\">Jason, Oct 2012</a></p>\n<p>More info <a title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/ \" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/%20\" target=\"_blank\">http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/</a></p>\n<p><a title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\">http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip</a> </p>\n<p><a title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_MP3_VOTEPACK.zip\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_MP3_VOTEPACK.zip\">http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_MP3_VOTEPACK.zip</a></p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p><span style=\"font-family:helvetica, 'helvetica neue', arial, sans-serif;font-size:12px;color:#333333;line-height:18px;\">This edition of LMM is a collaboration between myself and a group of middle school music students, many of whom started playing music only recently, under the direction of their instructor Jason Golday (author of LMM 1.8 - Burning Music). The process was a fairly simple one: Over the last academic year, the students have been writing pieces of music together, using what pitches they know (between five and seven different ones) on the available instruments (drums, glockenspiels, and recorders). Jason recorded these pieces and sent them to me. I manipulated them in various ways, adding voice and a few other sounds, paying close attention to the environmental elements of the recordings I had been given. In some cases, the sound of the space in which these pieces were initially performed is almost as important as the actual musical notes.<br /><br />It was Jason's idea to attempt this. I have to give him a big thanks for suggesting it. He heard early on the mesmerizing compositions his students were writing, and knew they were worth doing something more with. Once I started working on it, I too realized how strong and unique their musical concepts were. Really, the album was done before I ever got to it. I'm really happy with how it all turned out.<br /><br />-jw <br /></span></p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Arial; font-size: 9pt;\">The quirky genius of indie-pop songwriter Benjimanji was a gift he almost took for granted. Thankfully, close friends gave him the encouragement he needed to live up to his teen wunderkind talents. Benjimanji began as a bedroom indie rocker, recording lo-fi gems in his parent’s house as he attended the local university. While in school he scored an internship with the Air Force and found a handful of underground musical foils amongst a structured and bureaucratic environment.  One key ally has been sound engineer John Cody who encouraged Benjimanji to nurture his nascent talents through helping with the recording process. </p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Arial; font-size: 9pt;\"> </p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Arial; font-size: 9pt;\">Hallmarks of Benjimanji’s aesthetic include lavish orchestrations, Motown-via-1980s-new-wave bass lines, sharp hooks, playful irreverence, and a hint of world music. Benjimanji has garnered favorable comparisons to Vampire Weekend, Walk the Moon, Talking Heads, and the sweetly twisted world of filmmaker Wes Anderson.  </p>"
}

Supplied notices

{
  "albumInformation": "<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\">All of the tracks on this adventurous chip music compilation began with <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"monorave.wav\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/monowave.wav\" target=\"_blank\">a single sample</a>.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\">That's the sound of the <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"http://www.vacoloco.net/synths/monowave/\" href=\"http://www.vacoloco.net/synths/monowave/\" target=\"_blank\">Monowave</a>, a Moog clone originally envisioned as a bass synth.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\"><strong>Hexawe</strong>, a <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"Creative Commons - Attribution\" href=\"http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0\" target=\"_blank\">CC-BY</a> label for <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"http://littlegptracker.com/\" href=\"http://littlegptracker.com/\" target=\"_blank\">Piggy Tracker</a> releases, put out an open call for remixes. This group of talented musicians heeded the call, looping tiny sections of the monowave sample and sequencing these instruments using their portable game console of choice. The result is <strong>Monorave</strong>, an inspiring showcase of what's possible with remixed digital soundwaves.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\">This compilation is truly open source in that you can <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\" target=\"_blank\">download the tracker DAT files</a> yourself and tweak them. When you do, you'll find that each song has a folder containing all the samples used in the sequence, and many of the tracks draw all of their source material from that single monowave sample. -<a title=\"http://freemusicarchive.org/member/jason/blog/Monorave_Compilation\" href=\"/member/jason/blog/Monorave_Compilation\">Jason, Oct 2012</a></p>\n<p>More info <a title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/ \" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/%20\" target=\"_blank\">http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/</a></p>\n<p><a title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\">http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip</a> </p>\n<p><a title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_MP3_VOTEPACK.zip\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_MP3_VOTEPACK.zip\">http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_MP3_VOTEPACK.zip</a></p>"
}

Supplied notices

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>“<em>Laura’s music can be dark and a bit scary in places but live she has a wonderfully fun approach to her music. She’s like an episode of Twin Peaks in female form.</em>”</p>\n<p>-Aoife Barry (<a href=\"http://www.nialler9.com/2010/04/19/irish-week-aoife-barrys-top-5-irish-acts/\">Nialler9</a> Blog)</p>\n<p>I have been chasing Laura Sheeran to give me a release for Open for <em>literally</em> 3 years (beginning in my Net-Lab days). I heard her sing only once in person, for about 60 seconds, and I’ve been affected by it ever since.<br /> Be it her solo work, which runs the spectrum from naively sexual and gentle (in a <em>playing outside in the summer</em> kind of way) to immensely dark and tortured (<em>Trapped Under Ice</em> opens with the lyrics ‘<em>There’s panic in the atmosphere. My heart beats so fast, I cut through my tongue in fear…</em>‘), or her contributions with Fovea Hex, one cannot help but be blown away by the sheer (no pun intended) emotional weight of her output -where she waves her fingers, or quivers her lip, beautiful music gushes forth in dischordant waves of distress and comfort.</p>\n<p>And luckily for us, this release is no different. Featuring contributions from members of <strong>Fovea Hex</strong> and <strong>Nurse with Wound</strong> (we can’t believe it either!), plus some veterans of the Irish noise and outsider folk scenes, this is an all-too brief glimpse at amazing natural talent reaching upwards.</p>\n<p>- <a href=\"http://www.thisisopenmusic.com/release/music-for-the-deep-woods/\" target=\"_blank\">ThisIsOpenMusic!</a></p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>В преддверии заморского праздника Хэллоуин, рад представить свежий альбом петрозаводского хоррор-трио Voodoo Puppets, под названием Well To Hell.<br /> Это мощное цунами состоящего из агрессивного звука сносит за собой всех неравнодушных. Здесь переиграны практически все направления панк-рока, от сайкобилли до краста, завернутого в эстетику ужаса. <br /> К сожалению, больше не хватает слов, что бы выразить, насколько чертовски хороша данная пластинка. И я очень рад, что посчастливилось мне, выпустить её, хотя бы и в качестве цифровой версии.<br /><br />Recorded at Kukkovka Hell Studio<br />The sound producer - Dmitry \"Magister\" Lissitsky<br />Cover - Konstantin \"Rodi\" Rodionov</p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>In March of 2009, after slamming through the writing & recording of \"hey… that's not a Tootsie® Roll…\" in less than 9 days, we felt it would be really nice to just ONCE take a little more time making our next album... Not long after making that decision, as kirk was leaving the day job, he turned to his left and saw the sign pictured on the front cover. For some reason, he pulled out his crummy work phone, took the picture, went home, showed it to wendy - and we immediately knew the name of our next album. (And hey - now we even had a picture for a digitally downloadable book! Ooooo! Fancy!) And that's ALL we knew about \"last days last days.\" In April 2009 we went back into the studio & started writing the songs for \"last days last days;\" hell, we even had a bunch of songs already written. We thought that making this album would take us around... oh, 3 months. At most. Four years later, here it is. Following up on our founding principles (no two songs alike - ever; music should be a journey, not a destination; and the music always comes first), we had no idea what we would do. We just... Did It. And we only kept the songs that felt right - the end result being two of the songs we started with, and throwing out over 120 other songs we had written along the way. And not until we finally started putting together a track order did we discover that we had done the stupidest thing a band can do in The Age Of Single Downloads: we’d made a gapless, themed concept album - 15 or 16 Songs About Fear, Uncertainty, Doubt, Despair, Anger & Alienation. Y’know - Happy Stuff. And all of a sudden, that became the album’s subtitle - and it’s theme. But why that theme? What the hell was motivating all of this? We still don’t know; all we know is that the world we live in today has become cruel, unthinking, unfeeling & downright nasty; each of those things in the album’s subtitle brought to a fever pitch; each masterfully manipulated & motivated by Fear. Fear of Change. Fear of others. Fear of being left out. Fear of growing old. Fear of the Last Days. And we all need to do whatever we can just to get this world to Wake The Fuck Up. This album is our way of fighting back. The rest is up to You. It's your future. Go out & make a difference. ;) k&w p.s. mzkitty sez hicredits released 16 September 2013 _____________________________________________________ about this album: the narrative found-sound clips used in \"apathy\" came from \"Right or Wrong? (Making Moral Decisions),\" a 1951 Coronet Instructional Film in the public domain, and made available through the absolutely awesome Prelinger Archives (archive.org/details/prelinger), whom we humbly thank for their hours of astounding ephemeral films (check 'em out!) the monkeys in \"monkey\" all came from freesound, an amazing collaborative database of Creative Commons Licensed sounds. (www.freesound.org) the wonderful contributors were: soundbytez: (all licensed under creative commons attribution CC-BY) black-and-white-ruffed-lemurs siamangs lar-gibbon bidone: (public domain) bonobo monkeys in \"a meditation on the impending zombie apocalypse,\" there are women screaming at the beginning; since wendy can't scream, freesound again came to the rescue: thanvannispen: women-scream-aaa (licensed under creative commons attribution CC-BY) freqman: psycho-screams (licensed under creative commons attribution CC-BY) and we can't forget lonemonk's wonderful audience reaction we used in \"and a 21st century lullaby\": lonemonk_Audience_Reaction (licensed under creative commons attribution CC-BY) all other words & noises only slightly resembling music on this album were written, performed, recorded, fussed over, recorded again, fussed over some more, thrown out, recorded yet again and eventually wrestled to the ground, produced, mixed & mastered by kirk & wendy, aka another cultural landslide. (yes, making this album was really like that.) this album has been released under a Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported (CC-BY-3.0) license by another cultural landslide blah blah woof woof god bless our overly litigious society please feel free to share this music with anybody & everybody we would like to thank rob stewart of broken promise keeper (www.brokenpromisekeeper.com) for his excellent advice on how we could vaguely make something that only slightly resembled a powerpop song on \"monkey\" we would like to thank andrew dubber (andrewdubber.com) for listening as we spouted our incredibly off-the-wall ideas of what we feel needs to change in music and how we want to do it - and for not immediately thinking we were insane, but were instead just troublemakers we would also like to bow down & kiss the feet of rachel sclare - who not only took our stupid ideas for album & poster artwork & actually made them into something wonderful… but also did it all for free because she likes us; but then the thought of us bowing down & kissing her feet kind of grossed her out, so we'll just say: Thank You, Rachel. finally, we would like to thank You - our listener. you make this all worthwhile. it is our fondest wish that somehow, in some way, we've made you smile. kirk and wendy, aka acl, aka anothercultland, aka another cultural landslide p.s. in case you missed it earlier, mzkitty sez hi tagstags: alternative acl anothercultland anyandallrecords free free download free music nasty bastet other post-genre</p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\">All of the tracks on this adventurous chip music compilation began with <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"monorave.wav\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/monowave.wav\" target=\"_blank\">a single sample</a>.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\">That's the sound of the <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"http://www.vacoloco.net/synths/monowave/\" href=\"http://www.vacoloco.net/synths/monowave/\" target=\"_blank\">Monowave</a>, a Moog clone originally envisioned as a bass synth.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\"><strong>Hexawe</strong>, a <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"Creative Commons - Attribution\" href=\"http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0\" target=\"_blank\">CC-BY</a> label for <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"http://littlegptracker.com/\" href=\"http://littlegptracker.com/\" target=\"_blank\">Piggy Tracker</a> releases, put out an open call for remixes. This group of talented musicians heeded the call, looping tiny sections of the monowave sample and sequencing these instruments using their portable game console of choice. The result is <strong>Monorave</strong>, an inspiring showcase of what's possible with remixed digital soundwaves.</p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; padding: 8px 0px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 19px; font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', 'Lucida Grande', Arial, sans-serif; color: #222222;\">This compilation is truly open source in that you can <a style=\"color: #222222;\" title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\" target=\"_blank\">download the tracker DAT files</a> yourself and tweak them. When you do, you'll find that each song has a folder containing all the samples used in the sequence, and many of the tracks draw all of their source material from that single monowave sample. -<a title=\"http://freemusicarchive.org/member/jason/blog/Monorave_Compilation\" href=\"/member/jason/blog/Monorave_Compilation\">Jason, Oct 2012</a></p>\n<p>More info <a title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/ \" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/%20\" target=\"_blank\">http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/</a></p>\n<p><a title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip\">http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_DAT_VOTEPACK.zip</a> </p>\n<p><a title=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_MP3_VOTEPACK.zip\" href=\"http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_MP3_VOTEPACK.zip\">http://hexawe.net/compos/monorave/MONORAVE_MP3_VOTEPACK.zip</a></p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p><em>Walla walla</em> is the American term for atmospheric crowd background sounds in film and radio. In Japan, it is known as <em>gaya</em>, <em>rhubarb</em> the UK, <em>rhabarber</em> in Germany, and <em>rabarbar</em> in the Belguim, Netherlands, and Scandinavia.</p>\n<p><a href=\"http://www.filmsound.org/terminology/walla.htm\" target=\"_blank\">Film Sound</a> describes it in this way:</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">A sound effect for the murmur of a crowd in the background. </span><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">Walla is often use as subliminal aural communication and  sets a mood or a tone.</span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">The word <em>walla</em> was created in the old radio days when they needed the sound of a crowd in the background. They found if several people simply repeated \"walla, walla, walla, walla\"  it sounded like people talking. The audience did not really hear the words, just the buzz of voices.</span></p>\n</blockquote>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">Walla may be field recordings of crowds or staged by actors. This collection features actual groups and crowds recorded all over the world and generously donated for reuse at <a href=\"http://www.freesound.org\" target=\"_blank\">Freesound.org</a>. </span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">Such recordings may be helpful to and appreciated by FMA visitors creating audio and video productions. The recordings have been normalized, standardized for bitrates, tagged, and converted to mp3s from various other formats for this Free Music Archive collection. Please see individual tracks for licensing.<br /></span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\"> </span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\"><em>total time: 1:24:06</em><br /></span></p>\n<p><span style=\"font-family: Arial,Helvetica;\">cover painting </span><span class=\"fn\"><em>Манифестация 17 октября 1905 года<strong> (</strong></em></span><em>Demonstration on October 17, 1905) by Ilya Repin (1844-1930)</em><span class=\"fn\"><em><strong><br /></strong></em></span></p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p><span style=\"color: #222222; font-family: arial,sans-serif; font-size: 13px;\">Jordan Sinclair is a 24-year-old artist based in Los Angeles, California. Moving by way of Arizona, Jordan began building a name for himself following his graduation from Arizona State University.   Channeling his earliest influences from the midwest, Jordan’s first inspiration to write music was sparked by Eminem. Sinclair's sound carries a versatile use of new age and retro beat patterns. His debut release \"<em>Commerce</em>\" showcases Jordan's unique ability to maintain lyrical integrity over unique and dynamic production.  <br /></span></p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Home Recordings. Children singing, screaming and storytelling.</span></p>\n<p><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">All recordings are sourced from cassette tapes found in thrift stores and junk shops, tapes dubbed for us (from two of the kids featured here) and one tape was even found in a gutter! The only exception being the last track on this recording, by Grandpa Norm, singing to his grandson and we thought it fit quite nice on this compilation of home cassette recordings.</span><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Remember when you were a kid? Did you have a recorder? Even if you never held a microphone to your mouth and screamed making funny faces, I'm sure you can recall a time when you jumped around like a silly little monkey hooting and hollering. Maybe you still do! We hope so.</span><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><br style=\"box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\" /><span style=\"color: #333333; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px;\">Little is known on the background of these recordings. Estimated recording dates are from the early 1970's to the mid 1990's.</span></p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>To hear about future releases, you can join my mailing list, facebook or twitter from my website Axletreewood.com or the links on the artist page here, Thanks for listening :)</p>\n<p> </p>\n<p>Following the kind feedback from the first little EP, here is a second, recorded in the studio this time on a set of rare vintage microphones.</p>\n<p>These songs have emerged out of the spectacular autumn we've had in the UK, growing some vegetables and taking journeys through the countryside, past hamlets and streams, alive with the yellows and reds of the season.</p>\n<p>The artwork features a photo by Ailsa Naumann, (called 'witening wall'), who is also the inspiration for the second piece.</p>\n<p>Instagram: ailsa_naumann</p>\n<p>Enjoy, and feel free to let me know what you've used the pieces for :)</p>"
}

  "albumInformation": "<p>The album \"elevenandtwelve\" was born as a MIDI experiment in 2010. It’s nisei23's second full length release on rec72 and it’s worth that while! Because you’ll see drones and gravity’s rainbow after listening elevenandtwelve, that wild electronic shoe-gazer star. Most of the playing –  synths, pianos, guitars – has been improvised on an iPhone, recorded simultaneously on a computer and edited afterwards. nisei23′s album contains thirteen titles (+5o minutes).</p>"

{
  "albumInformation": "<p><strong>[fm.m02] </strong>field muzick mini cdr serie<br /></p><p>This psychoactive acoustical survey sets out to explore, under which  circumstances sounds and noises from the street cease to annoy.                               <br /><br /><em>»Like a sky-coloured Sunday-morning version of Kraftwerk’s \"Autobahn\".« Tocafi </em></p>\n<blockquote>\n<p>...These recordings took place at the IRCAM Paris in October of 2005. I  drove there in a Citroen CX. For whatever reason, the Plugins of my  Sequencer Software started to melt. This slowed down the recording  process in such a way, that I embarked on my journey home empty-handed.  Just like in a dream.</p>\n</blockquote>"
}

  "albumInformation": "<p><strong>\"Sunday Syndrome\" is a collection of soundscapes done in Spring and Summer of 2015.   The term \"syndrome\" is used to describe a combination of emotions, understandings, etc. that may be associated with, say, a specific day.   \"Earth Day Syndrome\", for example, conveys a sense of darkness associated with global warming, deforestation, extinctions, etc.   The album title conveys a sense of mellowness associated with a relaxing summer Sunday, as do many of these soundscapes.</strong></p>"

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>Traditional and ecstatic improvisations by L. Gonze</p>\n<p>A work in progress, permently. Songs being added as I make them, removed as my feelings change, or upgraded to better versions when I get an idea. This album will be finished when I stop making changes. But there is no definition of what it means to stop making changes.</p>\n<p>The idea for this series of recordings is:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Start with traditional acoustic americana. Take it out.</li>\n<li>Solo. Just one musician.</li>\n<li>When multitracking only one track has music. Others are found sounds.</li>\n<li>The music track is an improvisation. It's a single take from start to finish - no edits. For example, no comping parts from different takes.</li>\n<li>Introverted.</li>\n</ul>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>This was music I made for a friend (Luis). He is a car designer. I made some videos of him drawing cars and uploaded them on Youtube. The music was made to be used on these videos. We were exited. People were watching our videos. We would be rich and conquer the world! But then Luis got mad at me and now, for some reason, hates me. But the good thing is the music still remains.</p>\n<p>You are free to use this music in whatever way you like, because it is public domain (cc0 licence).</p>\n<p> </p>\n<p>• <a title=\"website\" href=\"https://marselmingablog.wordpress.com\" target=\"_blank\">https://marselmingablog.wordpress.com</a></p>\n<p>• <a title=\"my youtube channel\" href=\"http://www.youtube.com/c/MarselMingaVideo\" target=\"_blank\">Youtube</a></p>\n<p>• <a title=\"my flickr page\" href=\"http://www.flickr.com/photos/mars_\" target=\"_blank\">Flickr</a></p>"
}

{
  "track_information": "<div>We made our music available under the Creative Common license BY, but would like to add the non existing code ‘NAD'</div><p>NAD stands for \"No Audio Derivates’ In\n other words you can freely use (part of) our tracks in a film or video,\n but cannot remix or re-use part of our tracks in other musical work \nwithout our permission. We’d appreciate it if you could let us know \nwhere/when you used our music. <br><br>As an extra service we can make \ncustom edits or mixes for you. You can choose fragments, loops, solo-ed \ninstruments, remixes, etc.<br>Please feel free to contact us if you want to know more about using and/or customising our music  in your project.<span class=\"im\"><br></span></p>",
  "albumInformation": "<p>We made our music available under the Creative Common license BY, but would like to add the non existing code ‘NAD'NAD stands for \"No Audio Derivates’In other words you can freely use (part of) our tracks in a film or video, but cannot remix or re-use part of our tracks in other musical work without our permission. We’d appreciate it if you could let us know where/when you used our music.As an extra service we can make custom edits or mixes for you. You can choose fragments, loops, solo-ed instruments, remixes, etc.Please feel free to contact us if you want to know more about using and/or customising our music  in your project.</p>\n<p>Unheard Music Concepts: purely improvised instrumental music. A mixture of jazz, classical and minimal music with a touch of electronics.Unheard Music Concepts is a trio from the Netherlands consisting of Han Post (sax, clarinet), Marc Verhoeven (keys) and Daniel Talma (upright bass).They played together for many years in several groups (the Urge, Two Gentlemen, Masters & Johnson, Dutch Distress) and decided to go back to what they think is the core of all music: communication.They meet and play. They don't agree on chords, tempo or anything else. It is all about listening to and interacting with each other.Everything is recorded on a simple multitrack recorder, afterwards the best pieces are selected and mixed.Two albums have been released; Harbour (2015) and Industry (2016)</p>"
}

  "albumInformation": "<p>Started in March of 2009 by Jerry Cooper, an avid guitar player with 40+ years of experience. While blues is his main drive, any genre that uses a guitar can benefit from his creativity.Greg Pappas (originally born in Cancun, Mexico and now living in Zaragoza, Spain) was at this time the vocalist for this group. Known as the \"Chairman of the Board\" in Spain, he is known worldwide for his powerful vocals, inspiring lyrics, and speed painting. Please reference his videos on YouTube.Frank Nelson joined our group in August of 2009 with the intent of completing some projects which had become stalled. He helped put the projects together, reconstructing the drum tracks & adding keyboard tracks as necessary. Mixdown & mastering of the project was also handled by him.Greg left us a couple of months later. He stays pretty busy. But we managed to get noticed by another vocalist.Brad Wilson joined our group & did most of the vocals for the rest of this ongoing project. Ha also added some amazing harmonica tracks to a lot of our songs. He is currently a member of our band and we hope he stays with us for a long time to help us with our ongoing project.</p>"

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>Steve Combs and Simon Mathewson have expanded on the partnership resulting in their <a href=\"http://freemusicarchive.org/music/Steve_Combs/Notes/\"> Notes album</a>, yielding what we believe is the largest musical collaboration among Free Music Archive artists. Enlisting a dozen musicians with diverse backgrounds from the FMA, Steve set up a framework for random collaboration on the dozen tracks comprising the album. With three musicians per track, assigned to either start, continue or finish their piece, we present a set of audio <a href=\"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exquisite_corpse\">exquisite corpses</a>.</p>\n<p>To represent the random assemblage comprising the music, the album art is constructed with tiles provided by each participant.</p>\n<p>Produced, mixed and mastered by <a href=\"http://freemusicarchive.org/music/Lee_Rosevere/\" target=\"_self\">Lee Rosevere</a></p>\n<p><strong>I Know It’s Raining, Let’s Hug Anyway </strong>by Candlegravity, Unthunk, and simon_mathewson</p>\n<p><strong>If That’s What You Want</strong> by Steve Combs, half cocked, and Unthunk</p>\n<p><strong>Tessera</strong> by Blue Dot Sessions, Scott Holmes, and half cocked</p>\n<p><strong>Turkish Delight</strong> by half cocked, Blue Dot Sessions, and Small Colin (Ft. Lee Rosevere on drums)</p>\n<p><strong>Eat My Shorts</strong> by Scott Holmes, Small Colin, and Matt Oakley</p>\n<p><strong>Sleepless</strong> by Jahzzar, Candlegravity, and Blue Dot Sessions</p>\n<p><strong>Trident</strong> by simon_mathewson, Steve Combs, and Jahzzar</p>\n<p><strong>Unconquered Sun</strong> by Matt Oakley, simon_mathewson, and Scott Holmes</p>\n<p><strong>Loops To Aviemore</strong> by Small Colin, Matt Oakley, and Aglow Hollow</p>\n<p><strong>Mach Precedent</strong> by Aglow Hollow, Monk Turner, and Candlegravity</p>\n<p><strong>Baby Babble</strong> by Monk Turner, Aglow Hollow, and Steve Combs</p>\n<p><strong>Veronica’s Lament</strong> by Unthunk, Jahzzar, and Monk Turner</p>\n<p>The cover art was authored by the group as a collective, and is in the public domain under a CC0 license.</p>\n<p>For high-quality formats, download this album from the Bandcamp link.</p>"

Supplied notices

{
  "albumInformation": "<p style=\"margin:0px 0px 16px 0px;font:10px Verdana;\">Behind the Blind is eleven tracks of emotive, instrumental, electronica. This album comes highly recommended for fan's of Steve's other band, <a href=\"http://full-source.com/nosource/netlabel/artists_rho.htm\"><span style=\"text-decoration:underline;\">Rho</span></a>. The sound of Tardiss combines styles well developed by Boards of Canada and M83's early work. The first track Spinner, perfectly lays out the mood of the album. Fuzzy beats take lead as lovely synth work, plucked guitars, and percussive flares wash over them. Drill Bits is synth heavy romp that would not feel out of place on an early Boards of Canada album. Bicycle is the midway point of the album, featuring scratchy rhythms, strong chords, spacial guitar work, and spoken voice audio samples. Feathers and the Frail is a cinematic cold walk through abandoned streets. The album closes with Silver Fences, heartfelt end credits to a future metropolis.</p>\n "
}

  "albumInformation": "<p style=\"margin-bottom: 0.35cm; line-height: 115%;\"><span style=\"font-family: Arial,serif;\">Denavi Experience es un cassette editado en septiembre de 2015 en Santiago de Chile, una edición de 50 copias bajo la etiqueta Resistapes. Esta es la última producción musical del autodidacta Mauricio Romero, a través de su proyecto The Mugris.</span></p>\n<p style=\"margin-bottom: 0.35cm; line-height: 115%;\"><span style=\"font-family: Arial,serif;\">The Mugris es un proyecto de música electrónica atípico. Desde Talcahuano, las máquinas análogas se han hecho sentir con fuerza, y ya registra tres ediciones en cassette y un vinilo en 7” por tres sellos independientes: No Problema Tapes, Resistapes y BYM Records. Estos registros físicos hacen de The Mugris uno de los proyectos más prolíficos de la región del Biobío.</span></p>\n<p style=\"margin-bottom: 0.35cm; line-height: 115%;\"><br /><span lang=\"en\"><span>Denavi</span> <span>Experience</span> <span>is a</span> <span>cassette</span> <span>released in</span> <span>September 2015</span> <span>in Santiago,</span> <span>Chile,</span> <span>an edition of</span> <span>50 copies</span> <span>in the</span> <span>Resistapes</span> <span>label.</span> <span>This is the last</span> <span>musical</span> <span>production</span> <span>of</span> <span>self</span> <span>Mauricio</span> <span>Romero</span><span>, through</span> <span>his project The</span> <span>Mugris</span><span>.</span><br /><br /> <span>The</span> <span>Mugris</span> <span>is a project of</span> <span>unusual</span> <span>electronic music.</span> <span>From</span> <span>Talcahuano,</span> <span>analog</span> <span>machines</span> <span>have been felt</span> <span>strongly,</span> <span>and I</span> <span>recorded</span> <span>three editions</span> <span>in</span> <span>cassette</span> <span>and</span> <span>vinyl</span> <span>7</span> <span>\"for three</span> <span>independent labels</span><span>: No</span> <span>Problem</span> <span>Tapes</span><span>,</span> <span>Records</span> <span>Resistapes</span> <span>and</span> <span>BYM</span><span>.</span> <span>These</span> <span>physical records</span> <span>make The</span> <span>Mugris</span> <span>one of</span> <span>the most prolific</span> <span>projects in the</span> <span>Bio Bio region</span><span>.</span></span></p>"

{
  "albumInformation": "<p><span class=\"article_title_list\"><span class=\"article_title_list\"><b>File under:</b> Electronic Breakbeat Jazz</span></span></p><p><em>From the <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.allaboutjazz.com\">All About Jazz</a> review:</em><br /></p><p><span class=\"article_title_list\"><span class=\"article_title_list\">Combining \nelectronic breaks with jazz improvisation, <span style=\"text-decoration:underline;\">Effects of Elevation</span> is a \nunique example of the interesection where modern jazz and modern \nelectronic music meet.<br /><br />The release features guest musician \nMatthew Garrison on bass. Matt is known for his work with Herbie \nHancock, Joe Zawinul and others. Additionally, track 3 features vocal \nsamples by Ill-esha, known for her work as both a DJ and vocalist.</span></span></p><p> <em><a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.allaboutjazz.com/\">All About Jazz</a> writeup describes the remix, as well.</em><br /><span class=\"article_title_list\"><span class=\"article_title_list\"><br />Citizen\n Prime's remix combines a house groove with piano and bass solos on top.\n The airtight 4-to-the-floor rhythm propels the song as it progresses \nthrough solos, breakdowns and builds.<br /><br />The Sevenless remix \nincorporates IDM, glitch and industrial genres, while retaining a \ndistinctive sound. The remix begins slowly, eventually building into \nepic proportions with a guitar-laden breakbeat chorus.<br /><br /><em>EP info:</em><br /></span></span></p><p>Track 1 written and produced by Jonah Dempcy.\n  </p><p>Track 2 written and produced by <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.corkedfork.com\">Scott Baggett</a>.</p>\n  <p>Track 3 written and produced by <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://nicolas.manel.free.fr\">Nicolas Manel</a>.</p>\n  <p>Vocal sample on track 3 by <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.ill-esha.com\">Ill-esha</a>.</p>\n    <p>Cover art and design by <a target=\"_blank\" href=\"http://www.yurikomiyamoto.com\">Yuriko Miyamoto</a>.</p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Arial; font-size: 9pt;\">The quirky genius of indie-pop songwriter Benjimanji was a gift he almost took for granted. Thankfully, close friends gave him the encouragement he needed to live up to his teen wunderkind talents. Benjimanji began as a bedroom indie rocker, recording lo-fi gems in his parent’s house as he attended the local university. While in school he scored an internship with the Air Force and found a handful of underground musical foils amongst a structured and bureaucratic environment.  One key ally has been sound engineer John Cody who encouraged Benjimanji to nurture his nascent talents through helping with the recording process. </p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Arial; font-size: 9pt;\"> </p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0in; font-family: Arial; font-size: 9pt;\">Hallmarks of Benjimanji’s aesthetic include lavish orchestrations, Motown-via-1980s-new-wave bass lines, sharp hooks, playful irreverence, and a hint of world music. Benjimanji has garnered favorable comparisons to Vampire Weekend, Walk the Moon, Talking Heads, and the sweetly twisted world of filmmaker Wes Anderson.  </p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p style=\"margin: 0px; text-indent: 36.1px; font-size: 12px; font-family: Georgia;\">I traveled from the south of India to Nepal and back again in the winter and spring of 2015.  The experience changed my life.  As much of these recordings are an expression of the place and temperament that is India and Nepal, I believe in a way they tell somewhat of my story, too (though in a different language).  All recordings are raw; only the length of time was edited in any way.  </p>\n<p style=\"margin: 0px; text-indent: 36.1px; font-size: 12px; font-family: Georgia;\"><em>Volume I </em>is intimate.  Most songs were performed personally by musicians for me and are often playful or humorous. </p>"
}

{
  "albumInformation": "<p>“Poets and the Beast”, Mercury and the Architect’s break out EP, has taken the band a long way in a short time. From a first place showing in an international songwriting contest, to an invitation to perform live on the stage of the famous Bitter End,  this young band has been making its mark on the music scene in Manhattan for the past 6 months and truth be told,  they haven’t even begun yet.  Currently their break out LP is being produced and recorded at the famous Engine Room Studio with grammy award mastering engineer and studio owner Mark Christensen.  The songs and writing style of TJ Mercury can only be described as innovation wrapped in core tradition.  A new sound that embraces the philosophies of those who have come before with a prophet like vision of the future.”</p>"
}
